I will do it much the way I did before, with a few small changes only if the price and weather push me. I have farmed this land a long time, and I do not like taking chances at the start of the year. Around here, if wheat looks weak because fertilizer was cut too hard, that loss does not come back. So I will keep fertilizer on the safe side, not too fancy, just enough to hold yield. My land is 12 mu, and because my main way is wheat-maize, I will keep most land in that path and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Family labor is not as free as before since some people work outside, so I will keep the work simple: rotary tillage where it saves effort, well water when the crop really needs it, and sprays only when I see the field is starting to get taken by worms or disease. I watch what the men nearby do, and if most of them use one more bag and their field stands thicker, I do not want mine falling behind. So this year I will put 2 mu in cotton, 10 mu in wheat, and after wheat comes off those same 10 mu will go straight into maize.
